en.title: Minimum Cost to Merge Quality Classes So Equal Values Are Contiguous
en.description:
One operation chooses x and y and changes every x in the array to y, at a cost equal to the current number of occurrences of x. The goal is for the occurrences of each remaining value to form one contiguous segment; find the minimum total cost.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, and judging.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..200000), and the second line contains n quality values (−10⁹..10⁹).
en.explanation: Example 1: three values interleave within the same closed block; keep the 7 that appears 3 times and change the other 4 positions to 7, cost 4. Example 2: every class is already contiguous, cost 0. Example 3: change the middle 2 to 1, cost 1.
hints: Use last-occurrence positions to split the array into minimal closed blocks, similar to partitioning by each character's last position. All values in a block must be merged into one; keep the value with the highest original frequency in that block, cost = block length − maximum frequency.
